ev.c_first_steps.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} took {g=npc_sex:his|her} first steps: three steps from the hearth straight to you — then sat down hard, looking as if that had been the plan all along. The whole household clapped as if at the games.
ev.c_teething.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} screams night after night: the teeth are coming. The neighbor says rub the gums with honey, Grandmother says hang a wolf's tooth round the neck. You've tried both and are ready to bite someone yourself.
ev.c_amulet.text: {npc} now wears a charm against the evil eye. You spent longer choosing it than you once spent choosing a {g:wife|husband}.
ev.c_amulet.text.rome: {npc} now wears a {g=npc_sex:bulla, the round charm a Roman boy takes off only when he becomes a man|lunula, the little silver crescent a Roman girl takes off only before her wedding}. You spent longer choosing it than you once spent choosing a {g:wife|husband}.
ev.c_amulet.text.egypt: {npc} now wears an Eye of Horus in blue faience, against sickness and the evil eye. You spent longer choosing it than you once spent choosing a {g:wife|husband}.
ev.c_infant_fever.title: A Fever in the Cradle
ev.c_infant_fever.text: In the night your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is burning with fever and won't feed. So small a child, so great a fever. By morning you must decide where to run for help.
ev.c_infant_fever.physician.success: The physician said to sponge {g=npc_sex:him|her} with water and vinegar and not to bundle {g=npc_sex:him|her} up. By noon the fever broke, and you sat down for the first time that night.
ev.c_infant_fever.physician.failure: The physician shrugged and took his fee. The fever held for four days and left on its own — and you aged a year in those days.
ev.c_infant_fever.vow: Make a vow: if {g=npc_sex:he|she} lives, {g=npc_sex:he|she} will serve the temple
ev.c_infant_fever.vow.success: By dawn the fever eased. The vow has been spoken, and the gods, it seems, wrote it down.
ev.c_infant_fever.vow.failure: The fever lingered three more days, but it went in the end. A vow is still a vow.
ev.c_infant_fever.herbs: Send for the herb-woman and sit up all night
ev.c_infant_fever.herbs.success: Willow-bark tea, damp cloths, a quiet song until dawn. By morning {npc} is snuffling peacefully.
ev.c_infant_fever.herbs.failure: Five sleepless nights. The baby recovered; you can barely stand.
ev.c_vow_later.title: The Vow
ev.c_vow_later.text: The priests remind you: long ago, beside a sick child's cradle, you made a vow. {npc} has grown, and the temple is waiting for what was promised.
ev.c_vow_later.keep.ok: {npc} goes to the temple to sweep the courts, carry water and sing hymns. They say {g=npc_sex:he|she} is rather good at it.
ev.c_vow_later.pay: Redeem the vow with a rich gift
ev.c_vow_later.pay.ok: The temple accepted the gift — a new bronze tripod. The priest grumbled but declared the vow fulfilled.
ev.c_vow_later.forget.ok: You waved it away. But every time something breaks in the house, you can't help thinking it's no accident.
ev.c_nurse.title: The Wet Nurse
ev.c_nurse.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is a hungry baby, and the neighbors advise taking a wet nurse into the house. A good nurse isn't cheap, but every respectable family has one.
ev.c_nurse.hire.ok: The nurse turned out to be a grump, but she sings so well the whole house falls asleep.
ev.c_nurse.family.ok: The nights are short and your arms always full, but the baby knows the family's voices before anyone else's.
ev.c_nurse_later.title: The Old Nurse
ev.c_nurse_later.text: {npc} is all grown up, yet the old nurse still uses {g=npc_sex:his|her} baby nickname — in front of guests. Everyone laughs except {npc}.
ev.c_broken_amphora.title: The Broken Amphora
ev.c_broken_amphora.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} broke the amphora of your best wine and blamed the cat. The cat sits nearby, radiating contempt.
ev.c_broken_amphora.punish.ok: An evening with no sweets and a broom in hand. {npc} sulks; the cat gloats.
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh: Laugh — the wine was turning anyway
ev.c_broken_amphora.laugh.ok: The two of you swept up the shards, and the cat got a fish head by way of apology.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.success: After a long silence {npc} mumbled, "It was me." You forgave {g=npc_sex:him|her} at once — for the courage.
ev.c_broken_amphora.truth.failure: {npc} stuck to the story until the tears came. The cat's name was never cleared.
ev.c_honest_later.title: An Honest Word
ev.c_honest_later.text: They say {npc} refused to short-weigh a customer, even when told to. The boss was furious — and now that customer deals with no one else. You remember a broken amphora and a cat.
ev.c_fear_dark.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is afraid of the dark: the old woman next door told stories of Lamia, who steals naughty children. Now a lamp burns by the bed all night, and the oil goes as if it were a festival.
ev.c_pet.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} brought home a tortoise and named it after you. The household sees the resemblance: just as unhurried and just as stubborn.
ev.c_pet.text.rome: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} raised a jackdaw chick, and it learned exactly one word: "Ave!" Now it hails every guest like a general in triumph, and the guests don't know where to look.
ev.c_pet.text.egypt: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} lured a kitten into the house. In Egypt the cat is a sacred animal, so the house has a new master — and it sleeps in your spot.
ev.c_toys.text: You made a little wooden horse on wheels. Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} pulls it around from dawn to dusk and feeds it barley — real barley, from your stores.
ev.c_mischief.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} drew the neighbor in charcoal right on the wall of his house — a very good likeness. The neighbor recognized himself and hasn't said hello to you for a week.
ev.c_mischief.text.2: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} fed the neighbor's goat the cakes baked for the household altar. The goat is pleased. Hopefully the gods are too.
ev.c_mischief.text.3: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} traded your best sandals for a handful of nuts and a dead beetle. Both parties consider the deal fair — everyone except you.
ev.c_question.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} asked why the gods never come to dinner, since food is always left out for them. You had no answer and ate the cake yourself.
ev.c_question.text.2: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} asked where the sun goes at night and whether it gets scared there all alone. You spent half the evening explaining and the other half comforting.
ev.c_river.title: By the Water
ev.c_river.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} ran off to the river with the neighbors' children without asking and slipped on the rocks. A fisherman hauled {g=npc_sex:him|her} out by the collar — soaked, terrified and very proud of {g=npc_sex:himself|herself}.
ev.c_river.teach: Teach {g=npc_sex:him|her} to swim, since the water calls
ev.c_river.teach.ok: All summer you splashed about in the evenings. By autumn {npc} swims like a fish and frightens you in brand-new ways.
ev.c_river.forbid.ok: {npc} sulks. Now {g=npc_sex:he|she} sneaks off to the river in secret — but at least not alone.
ev.c_river.thank: Thank the fisherman and let it go
ev.c_river.thank.ok: The fisherman left with a jug of wine. You went on flinching at the word "river" for a long time.
ev.c_swim_later.title: Pulled from the Water
ev.c_swim_later.text: A boat capsized on the river, and {npc} was the first into the water. The two who were pulled out now bow when they meet you — and you remember those summer evenings by the river.
ev.c_child_fall.title: A Broken Arm
ev.c_child_fall.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} climbed the old olive tree by the road and fell. The arm is swollen and hangs wrong. {g=npc_sex:He|She} is trying very hard not to cry.
ev.c_child_fall.physician: Take {g=npc_sex:him|her} to a physician to set and splint it
ev.c_child_fall.physician.ok: The physician set the bone in one movement — the whole street heard the scream — and splinted it. Two months later the arm was as good as new.
ev.c_child_fall.bonesetter: Fetch the bonesetter from the market
ev.c_child_fall.bonesetter.success: The bonesetter pulled, muttered something and tied on a board. It healed straight.
ev.c_child_fall.bonesetter.failure: It healed crooked: that arm is weaker now. {npc} insists it's a battle wound.
ev.c_child_fall.pray.success: A board, a rag and a prayer — the arm healed. You promised the gods a rooster and kept your word.
ev.c_child_fall.pray.failure: The gods must have been busy: the arm healed crooked. {npc} insists it's a battle wound.
ev.c_lost.text: At the festival your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} got lost in the crowd. You spent half the day rushing round the market — and found the runaway by the temple, front row, mouth open, listening to a storyteller.
ev.c_knucklebones.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} beat you at knucklebones five times running. On the sixth you noticed {g=npc_sex:his|her} bones were suspiciously obedient.
ev.c_teacher.title: The Teacher's Complaint
ev.c_teacher.text: The teacher complains that your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} counts flies instead of letters and has had the rod twice already. {npc} insists the teacher is simply mean.
ev.c_teacher.teacher.ok: There's more tablet work at home now. {npc} grumbles, but the letters have got straighter.
ev.c_teacher.new_teacher: Find a kinder teacher, even a pricier one
ev.c_teacher.new_teacher.ok: The new teacher teaches letters with honey biscuits: learn your alpha, eat your alpha. Lessons are going well.
ev.c_teacher.home_teach.ok: In the evenings the two of you sit over the tablet. You've discovered you'd long forgotten half the letters yourself.
ev.c_bully.title: The Bully
ev.c_bully.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came home with a split lip: the butcher's son, a head taller, has been taking {g=npc_sex:his|her} bread for days.
ev.c_bully.fight.success: A week later the butcher's son came home with a split lip of his own. Nobody touches the bread now.
ev.c_bully.fight.failure: Hitting back worked — but the butcher's son hit back twice as hard. More bruises, but less fear.
ev.c_bully.parents: Have a word with the butcher
ev.c_bully.parents.success: The butcher listened, turned purple and gave his son such a hiding that the boy now crosses the street when he sees your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter}.
ev.c_bully.parents.failure: The butcher laughed: kids sort these things out themselves. And ever since, your meat comes with extra bone.
ev.c_bully.avoid.ok: {npc} now goes the long way round, through the market. A longer road, and a longer grudge.
ev.c_bully_later.title: The Childhood Enemy
ev.c_bully_later.text: {npc} and the butcher's son — that very bully — now sell sausages together, and do well at it, they say. You can't remember when they became friends. Probably during that fight.
ev.c_talent.title: A Gift
ev.c_talent.text: A music teacher heard your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} singing at chores and asks to take {g=npc_sex:him|her} as a pupil: "A voice like that comes once in a generation." Lessons aren't cheap.
ev.c_talent.lessons.ok: Now lyre practice drifts from the house every evening. The neighbors are split between the enchanted and the exhausted.
ev.c_talent.choir: Send {g=npc_sex:him|her} to the temple choir — free, but strict
ev.c_talent.choir.ok: The choirmaster is strict and stingy with praise. {npc} comes home hoarse, but sings better and better.
ev.c_talent.free: Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} sing for fun — songs don't feed anyone
ev.c_talent.free.ok: {npc} sings as before — at work, at the well, in {g=npc_sex:his|her} sleep. Free of charge.
ev.c_talent_later.title: A Voice at the Festival
ev.c_talent_later.text: At the great festival {npc} sang before the whole city. The crowd fell silent, then roared. You stood at the back pretending you had something in your eye.
ev.c_figs.title: Stolen Figs
ev.c_figs.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came home with a lap full of figs — and the neighbor right behind, holding the little thief by the ear and demanding justice.
ev.c_figs.text.athens: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} came home with a lap full of figs — and the neighbor right behind, holding the little thief by the ear and demanding justice. They say that's why Athenian informers are called sycophants — "fig-showers".
ev.c_figs.pay: Pay up and send {g=npc_sex:him|her} to work it off in his orchard
ev.c_figs.pay.ok: For three days {npc} weeded the neighbor's beds. {g=npc_sex:He|She} can't stand the sight of figs now.
ev.c_figs.defend: Stand up for {g=npc_sex:him|her}: half his figs rot anyway
ev.c_figs.defend.ok: The neighbor left, cursing loud enough for the whole block. {npc} looks at you like a hero, and you ate the figs together.
ev.c_figs.dinner: Invite the neighbor to dinner — figs included
ev.c_figs.dinner.success: By the end of dinner the neighbor was roaring with laughter and inviting the little thief to help with the harvest.
ev.c_figs.dinner.failure: The neighbor didn't see the funny side and left, slamming the door. He did leave the figs, though.
ev.c_help_work.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} helped you at work for the first time — very serious, tongue sticking out. Little was ruined, and there was enough pride to last the whole evening.
ev.c_rebellion.title: Out at Night
ev.c_rebellion.text: For the third night running your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has come home near dawn, smelling of wine and talking back: "I'm not a child anymore!" The neighbors saw {g=npc_sex:him|her} with company best not mentioned.
ev.c_rebellion.strict: Keep {g=npc_sex:him|her} home and pile on the work
ev.c_rebellion.strict.ok: A month under house watch. {npc} says nothing and glowers, but sleeps at home.
ev.c_rebellion.talk.success: You talked until dawn. It turns out {g=npc_sex:he's|she's} simply afraid of becoming as boring as you. That stung, and it was honest.
ev.c_rebellion.talk.failure: The talk ended with a slammed door. You talked too long and listened too little.
ev.c_rebellion.freedom: Remember yourself at that age and let go
ev.c_rebellion.freedom.ok: {npc} appreciates the trust — and makes the most of it. You lie awake till dawn, listening for footsteps.
ev.c_first_love.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is in love: sighing, not eating, writing someone's name on every wall. You never knew your house had so many walls.
ev.c_teen_wrestle.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} challenged you to arm-wrestling — and won. You said you let {g=npc_sex:him|her} win. No one believed it, including you.
ev.c_coming_of_age.text: One morning you noticed {npc} is no longer a child: a different voice, arguments about grain prices, and embarrassment when you ruffle {g=npc_sex:his|her} hair.
ev.c_coming_of_age.text.rome: {npc} {g=npc_sex:put on the white toga of a grown man for the first time and took off his childhood bulla|laid her dolls on the household altar — the way Roman girls say goodbye to childhood}. You watched and couldn't understand where the years had gone.
ev.c_coming_of_age.text.athens: {npc} {g=npc_sex:cut off his boyhood curls and offered them to the gods, as Athenians do at the Apaturia festival|dedicated her childhood toys to Artemis — the way Athenian girls say goodbye to childhood}. You watched and couldn't understand where the years had gone.
ev.c_trade.title: Which Trade
ev.c_trade.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} is growing up, and it's time to decide which trade to set {g=npc_sex:him|her} to. {npc} looks at you and waits — or perhaps waits for you to ask what {g=npc_sex:he|she} wants.
ev.c_trade.craft.ok: The master has a new apprentice: {npc} is up before dawn and comes home with burnt fingers and shining eyes.
ev.c_trade.scribe: Letters and accounts — train as a scribe
ev.c_trade.scribe.ok: {npc} now carries wax tablets under one arm and looks at you a little condescendingly: you, after all, can't spell.
ev.c_trade.merchant: Place {g=npc_sex:him|her} with a merchant you know
ev.c_trade.merchant.ok: {npc} is learning to haggle, to weigh, and to praise the goods with an honest face. They say that last part needed hardly any teaching.
ev.c_trade.free.ok: {npc} promised to think it over — and has been thinking for two weeks now, lying on the roof. But {g=npc_sex:he|she} looks at you like a grown-up now.
ev.c_trade_high.title: A Path for Your {g=npc_sex:Son|Daughter}
ev.c_trade_high.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has grown up. Friends advise: serving the gods brings honor, Greek medicine brings respect and income, the family estates bring security. The choice is yours — but {npc} already has opinions.
ev.c_trade_high.priest.ok: The priests welcomed the new acolyte with honor — and with hopes of generous gifts from the family.
ev.c_trade_high.physician.ok: {npc} spends every day with the physician, memorizing herbs and bones and alarming the family with stories at dinner.
ev.c_trade_high.estates.ok: {npc} rides round the estates, counting olive trees and arguing with the stewards. The stewards already miss the old days.
ev.c_trade_high.free.ok: {npc} was silent a long while, then said, "Thank you." That seemed to matter more than any choice.
ev.c_trade_later.title: Master of the Trade
ev.c_trade_later.text: {npc} has become someone known by name in the trade: clients ask for {g=npc_sex:him|her} specifically and pay without haggling. You act as if you always believed it.
ev.c_wedding.title: Your {g=npc_sex:Son's|Daughter's} Wedding
ev.c_wedding.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son's|daughter's} wedding is near. {npc} is glowing, the in-laws are waiting, and the neighbors are guessing how generous you'll be: {g=npc_sex:the feast for the whole street is on you|the dowry is yours to provide, and the whole family will be judged by it}.
ev.c_wedding.lavish.ok: Flute girls, torches, a mountain of honey cakes. The street talked about this wedding until the next one.
ev.c_wedding.modest.ok: The wedding was quiet and warm. The in-laws pursed their lips, but the young couple didn't even notice.
ev.c_wedding.borrow: Borrow from a moneylender and do it in style
ev.c_wedding.borrow.ok: Everyone remembered the wedding — the moneylender most of all.
ev.c_wedding_debt_later.title: The Wedding Debt
ev.c_wedding_debt_later.text: The moneylender has come about the wedding debt — with interest that has grown over the years like a child. {npc} offers to help pay.
ev.c_wedding_debt_later.pay.ok: You counted out the coins and, for the first time in years, breathed easy.
ev.c_wedding_debt_later.together.ok: {npc} silently put a purse on the table. You split the debt down the middle — and it brought you closer than the wedding itself.
ev.c_far_away.title: The Far Road
ev.c_far_away.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} wants to leave: {g=npc_sex:sign on with a trading ship or the army and see the world|go with her husband to a distant colony where his family has a business}. Promises to come back rich. You recall that everyone promises that.
ev.c_far_away.bless: Give your blessing and money for the road
ev.c_far_away.bless.ok: You stood on the shore until the sail was a dot. The house has become far too quiet.
ev.c_far_away.let_go: Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} go without money — make {g=npc_sex:his|her} own way
ev.c_far_away.let_go.ok: {npc} left with one small bundle and your advice. The advice, you hope, weighs more.
ev.c_far_away.forbid: Forbid it: {g=npc_sex:his|her} place is at home
ev.c_far_away.forbid.ok: {npc} stayed. But in the evenings {g=npc_sex:he|she} gazes at the road for a long time, and you pretend not to notice.
ev.c_far_return.title: The Return
ev.c_far_return.text: {npc} is back — tanned, full of foreign words, with a sack of gifts: for you, {g:a bone-handled knife|a string of beads from a faraway sea}, and for everyone, stories till dawn.
ev.c_debts.title: Your {g=npc_sex:Son's|Daughter's} Debts
ev.c_debts.text: Men with heavy fists have come calling: your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} owes a moneylender more than {g=npc_sex:he|she} earns in a year — and told him the family would pay.
ev.c_debts.pay.ok: The debt is cleared. {npc} swears by all the gods it will never happen again. You'd very much like to believe it.
ev.c_debts.half: Pay half — the rest {g=npc_sex:he|she} works off
ev.c_debts.half.ok: {npc} worked a year without holidays. Grumbled, but forgot the way to the moneylender's door.
ev.c_debts.refuse.ok: {npc} sold everything {g=npc_sex:he|she} owned and didn't show up at your door for a long time.
ev.c_debts_again.title: Debts Again
ev.c_debts_again.text: {npc} is in debt again — and again swears it's the last time. Same eyes, same oaths, just a bigger sum.
ev.c_debts_again.pay.ok: You paid. But deep down you already know this time isn't the last.
ev.c_debts_again.cut: Say it: not one more coin
ev.c_debts_again.cut.ok: The words came hard. But half a year later {npc} came by — asking for nothing, just with a basket of apples.
ev.c_business.title: A Business of {g=npc_sex:His|Her} Own
ev.c_business.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} turns up with shining eyes, wanting to open {g=npc_sex:a bakery|a cloth shop} by the market. All that's missing is money. Yours.
ev.c_business.give.ok: You counted out the coins, and {npc} hugged you the way {g=npc_sex:he|she} hadn't since childhood.
ev.c_business.partner: Go in as a partner — half the money, but a say in things
ev.c_business.partner.ok: It's agreed: half the money, half the profit, and the advice free of charge. {npc} sighed, but agreed.
ev.c_business.refuse.ok: {npc} left without a word. They say {g=npc_sex:he|she} took work in someone else's shop — to save up alone.
ev.c_business_good.title: Business Is Good
ev.c_business_good.text: There's a queue outside your {g=npc_sex:son's|daughter's} shop every morning. {npc} paid back your money and then some — and sends a basket of the best goods every holiday.
ev.c_business_bad.title: Gone Under
ev.c_business_bad.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son's|daughter's} business has gone under: the partner ran off, the stock got damp, the debts remain. {npc} sits in your kitchen, unable to look up.
ev.c_business_bad.comfort.ok: You poured some wine and told {g=npc_sex:him|her} about your own failures. There turned out to be a surprising number.
ev.c_business_bad.reproach.ok: You were right. It brought no joy whatsoever.
ev.c_law.title: Trouble with the Law
ev.c_law.text: A neighbor has gone to court: your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc}, he says, broke a jug over his head at the tavern. {npc} swears the neighbor started it. Half the tavern saw it, and each tells a different story.
ev.c_law.pay.ok: The neighbor got enough for his treatment — enough for three such heads. The case was dropped.
ev.c_law.patron: Ask an influential acquaintance to step in
ev.c_law.patron.success: The influential acquaintance had a word in the right ear. The neighbor suddenly recalled that he'd fallen on the jug himself.
ev.c_law.patron.failure: The acquaintance spread his hands. You had to pay the fine — and pretend you weren't hurt.
ev.c_law.answer.ok: The court ordered a fine and a month's work for the neighbor. {npc} worked it all off — and barely spoke to you.
ev.c_lesson_later.title: A Lesson Learned
ev.c_lesson_later.text: One evening at dinner {npc} suddenly said, "Back then I hated you. Now I understand: if you'd bailed me out, I'd never have learned a thing."
ev.c_pride.text.1: At the market a stranger, not knowing who you were, went on and on praising a {g=npc_sex:craftsman|craftswoman} named {npc}. You nodded in silence — then at home told everyone. Three times.
ev.c_pride.text.2: For no reason at all your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} brought you a gift — bought with {g=npc_sex:his|her} own money, earned at {g=npc_sex:his|her} own trade. As gifts go it's so-so, but it sits in the place of honor.
ev.c_pride.text.3: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} settled a quarrel between two neighbors so wisely that both went away happy. You don't remember teaching that — so it must have grown on its own.
ev.c_new_faith.title: A New Teaching
ev.c_new_faith.text: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} has taken up a new teaching: goes to gatherings at night, talks of saving the soul and looks at the household gods with pity.
ev.c_new_faith.text.rome: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} now worships some eastern goddess: wears white linen, fasts before the rites and says the Roman gods are for people who've never seen true mysteries.
ev.c_new_faith.text.athens: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} trails after a wandering philosopher: barefoot, in an old cloak, arguing with everyone in the agora and insisting that wealth is a burden and family custom an empty habit.
ev.c_new_faith.accept: Accept it: everyone seeks their own gods
ev.c_new_faith.accept.ok: You argue at dinner, but without malice. Sometimes {g=npc_sex:he|she} even comes to the household altar — to keep you company.
ev.c_new_faith.forbid: Forbid it, and threaten the inheritance
ev.c_new_faith.forbid.ok: {npc} packed up. "So that's how it is," {g=npc_sex:he|she} said, and left.
ev.c_new_faith.listen.ok: You sat all night among strangers and strange words. You didn't understand all of it — but you understood your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} better.
ev.c_faith_reconcile.title: Years Later
ev.c_faith_reconcile.text: {npc} stands at the door — older, with the same stubborn line at the mouth as yours. "I haven't given up my faith," {g=npc_sex:he|she} says. "But I haven't given up on you either."
ev.c_faith_reconcile.embrace.ok: You talked until morning. Not a word about faith.
ev.c_faith_reconcile.terms: Let {g=npc_sex:him|her} in — but no talk of faith in this house
ev.c_faith_reconcile.terms.ok: Now you dine together on holidays and politely say nothing about what matters most. That's peace too.
ev.c_visit_old.text.1: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} turned up unannounced — with a basket of food and some tools — and spent the day fixing your leaky roof. Refused any payment, and scolded you for not asking sooner.
ev.c_visit_old.text.2: Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} now drops by every evening — "just passing." Passing, it turns out, from the other side of town.
ev.c_old_care.title: Under One Roof
ev.c_old_care.text: Your legs obey you less and less, and the house feels bigger every year. Your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} offers: "Come and live with us. There's room, everyone would be glad, and I'd stop worrying."
ev.c_old_care.move.ok: They gave you the best corner by the hearth. Noisy, crowded — and for the first time in years, falling asleep isn't frightening.
ev.c_old_care.stay: Stay in your own home while your legs still carry you
ev.c_old_care.stay.ok: {npc} sighed, and now comes by every other day. You grumble, but you wait for it.
ev.c_old_care.help.ok: The helper sings loudly and sweeps badly, but you're no longer alone in the house.
ev.c_grand_first_hold.text: You held your {g=npc_sex:grandson|granddaughter} for the first time — and {npc} promptly grabbed your nose and wouldn't let go. The parents say {g=npc_sex:he|she} takes after you.
ev.c_grand_spoil.title: {g:Grandpa's|Grandma's} Treats
ev.c_grand_spoil.text: Your {g=npc_sex:grandson|granddaughter} {npc} whispers a request for a honey cake — and a toy chariot. The parents have strictly forbidden spoiling.
ev.c_grand_spoil.spoil: Buy it all — that's what {g:grandfathers|grandmothers} are for
ev.c_grand_spoil.spoil.ok: The chariot is hidden under your bed, and the cake was eaten on the spot. It's your shared secret.
ev.c_grand_spoil.obey.ok: {npc} pouted, but by evening the grudge was forgotten and {g=npc_sex:he|she} fell asleep curled up beside you.
ev.c_grand_spoil.build: Instead of buying one — build the chariot together
ev.c_grand_spoil.build.ok: The chariot came out crooked, but it's theirs. {npc} shows it to everyone: "{g:Grandpa|Grandma} and me made it!"
ev.c_grand_craft_later.title: The Crooked Chariot
ev.c_grand_craft_later.text: {npc} is nearly grown and makes things better than you do. One day {g=npc_sex:he|she} admitted it all started with that crooked chariot the two of you built.
ev.c_grand_story.text: Your {g=npc_sex:grandson|granddaughter} {npc} asked about your youth. With every retelling the story gains more bandits, storms and heroics. Soon you'll believe it yourself.
ev.c_grand_mischief.text: Your {g=npc_sex:grandson|granddaughter} {npc} hid your walking stick and spent half the day innocently helping you look for it. It turned up down the well. {npc} insists it fell in by itself.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.title: Marsh Fever
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.text: A rotten damp drifts in from the marshes outside the city, and the fever has you: a day of burning, two days' respite, then burning again. The neighbors say wear a charm round your neck; the Greek physician says bitter draughts and sleep far from the low ground.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.physician.ok: Bitter draughts, sleeping upstairs, no wine at all. A month later the fever loosened its grip.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.hills: Go up into the hills, to the dry air
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.hills.ok: The hills are cool, there are no mosquitoes, and the mornings smell of thyme. You came back healthy and tanned.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.charm.success: Round your neck hangs a scrap of papyrus with words you don't understand. The fever evidently did, and left.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.charm.failure: The charm didn't help. The fever turns up on its day like a tax collector.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.work.success: You worked on the fever-free days and lay down on the others. By autumn the illness gave out before you did.
ev.c_h_marsh_fever.work.failure: You didn't give in, and neither did the fever. So far the score is in its favor.
ev.c_h_eye.title: Eye Sickness
ev.c_h_eye.text: Sand, sun and flies have done their work: your eyes are swollen, weeping and burning. Egyptian eye doctors are famous across the world — and charge accordingly.
ev.c_h_eye.doctor.ok: The doctor washed your eyes, applied a honey salve and told you to sit in the dark for three days. The world came back — brighter than before.
ev.c_h_eye.kohl: Line your eyes thickly with green paint, as Grandmother taught, and pray to Horus
ev.c_h_eye.kohl.success: Green paint, a prayer — and in a week your eyes were clear. Grandmother was right, as always.
ev.c_h_eye.kohl.failure: The paint didn't help. Your eyes kept weeping for a long time, and your sight got worse.
ev.c_h_eye.endure: Put up with it — it'll pass
ev.c_h_eye.endure.success: It passed. A week later you couldn't remember what you'd been worried about.
ev.c_h_eye.endure.failure: It didn't pass. Your eyes wept for a long time, and something in them has been cloudy ever since.
ev.c_h_eyes_later.title: Fading Sight
ev.c_h_eyes_later.text: Letters blur, and at the market you know faces only by their voices. The old eye sickness has come back to remind you.
ev.c_h_wound.title: A Festering Wound
ev.c_h_wound.text: A trifling scratch from a rusty nail has swollen and reddened in a week and throbs so hard you can't sleep. Your arm is hot right up to the elbow.
ev.c_h_wound.physician: Let a physician lance and cauterize it
ev.c_h_wound.physician.ok: It hurt so much you'll remember the physician's face for the rest of your life. But a week later the arm was as good as new.
ev.c_h_wound.honey: Wash it with wine and dress it with honey, as the old folks did
ev.c_h_wound.honey.success: Wine, honey, a clean cloth twice a day. The wound closed — the old folks knew what they were doing.
ev.c_h_wound.honey.failure: The honey didn't help: the wound festered for another month and took a lot out of you.
ev.c_h_wound.temple: Take a clay arm to the temple — that's how you ask the gods for healing
ev.c_h_wound.temple.success: The clay arm now hangs in the temple among hundreds of others. Your real one has healed.
ev.c_h_wound.temple.failure: There are hundreds of clay arms in the temple. Yours evidently hasn't come up yet.
ev.c_h_stomach.title: A Bad Stomach
ev.c_h_stomach.text: Maybe the market fish was yesterday's, maybe the well water has gone bad — but your stomach is so wrung out that for three days you haven't strayed far from home.
ev.c_h_stomach.barley: Fast and drink barley water, as physicians advise
ev.c_h_stomach.barley.success: Three days on barley water and your stomach settled. The first flatbread afterwards tasted like a feast.
ev.c_h_stomach.barley.failure: The barley water didn't help. The sickness hangs on and wears you down to the bone.
ev.c_h_stomach.purge: Let the physician give you a purge
ev.c_h_stomach.purge.success: The remedy was awful and the night even worse, but by morning the sickness was gone.
ev.c_h_stomach.purge.failure: The remedy proved stronger than the illness. The sickness left — and very nearly took you with it.
ev.c_h_stomach.pray: Pray, and drink only from the temple spring
ev.c_h_stomach.pray.success: Clean water and prayer did their work: on the fifth day you were back on your feet.
ev.c_h_stomach.pray.failure: The gods are in no hurry. The sickness drags on.
ev.c_h_cough.title: The Cough That Won't Go
ev.c_h_cough.text: The cough has hung on since winter and has no intention of leaving: at night your chest feels stuffed with wool. The physician shakes his head and advises what he advises all wealthy patients — a sea voyage and dry air.
ev.c_h_cough.voyage.ok: A month on deck, salt wind, the dry sun of foreign shores. You came back without the cough and with a pile of stories.
ev.c_h_cough.rest: Rest it out: honey, warm milk, quiet
ev.c_h_cough.rest.success: A month under the blanket and the cough gave up. The household swears you fussed more than you coughed.
ev.c_h_cough.rest.failure: A month under the blanket didn't help. The cough got quieter, but it didn't leave.
ev.c_h_cough.work: Keep working — no time to be ill
ev.c_h_cough.work.success: The cough gave up on you and went off to someone more obliging.
ev.c_h_cough.work.failure: The work goes on, and so does the cough. You don't sleep at night and can barely stand by day.
ev.c_h_tooth.title: Toothache
ev.c_h_tooth.text: The tooth has ached three nights running, your cheek is swollen, and you'd give anything to whoever makes it stop. There's a tooth-puller at the market, as it happens.
ev.c_h_tooth.pull: Off to the tooth-puller at the market
ev.c_h_tooth.pull.ok: Pincers, strong hands, one short howl — the onlookers at the market even applauded. The pain left with the tooth.
ev.c_h_tooth.physician: To a physician — maybe the tooth can be saved
ev.c_h_tooth.physician.success: The physician let out the pus, rinsed the gum with wine and left the tooth in place. You chewed with it for many more years.
ev.c_h_tooth.physician.failure: The physician fussed for ages and then pulled it anyway. Just three times the price.
ev.c_h_tooth.endure: Rinse with vinegar and grit your teeth
ev.c_h_tooth.endure.success: A week later the swelling went down. The tooth has gone quiet — for now.
ev.c_h_tooth.endure.failure: The swelling spread across your whole cheek and the fever came. You can't put up with it any longer.
ev.c_h_bone.title: A Broken Leg
ev.c_h_bone.text: You slipped on wet steps and heard a crack. The leg is swelling before your eyes, and you can't put any weight on it.
ev.c_h_bone.physician: A physician with splints and traction
ev.c_h_bone.physician.ok: The physician pulled, measured and bandaged for a long time. Two months in bed — and the leg healed straight.
ev.c_h_bone.bonesetter.success: The bonesetter yanked, you howled, the bone went back in place. Cheap and cheerful.
ev.c_h_bone.bonesetter.failure: The bone knit, but not quite the way nature intended.
ev.c_h_bone.self: Tie on a board and lie still
ev.c_h_bone.self.success: You lay in bed for two months, driving the household mad. The leg healed.
ev.c_h_bone.self.failure: The leg healed crooked. You walk again — but not the way you used to.
ev.c_h_limp_later.title: A Limp
ev.c_h_limp_later.text: The old break makes itself felt: you limp, and you climb stairs sideways like a crab. The boys in the street imitate you — without malice, but spot on.
ev.c_h_plague.title: Rumors of Pestilence
ev.c_h_plague.text: At the harbor they talk of a ship where half the rowers died of fever. Two people in the next quarter have already taken to their beds. The city whispers, and every cough sounds like a sentence.
ev.c_h_plague.leave: Leave for the countryside until it dies down
ev.c_h_plague.leave.ok: You waited it out with relatives in the country. The rumors turned out worse than the illness: few in the city fell sick.
ev.c_h_plague.stay: Stay: fumigate the house, wash with vinegar, keep away from the harbor
ev.c_h_plague.stay.success: The house reeks of sulfur and vinegar, but the pestilence passed you by.
ev.c_h_plague.stay.failure: For all your care, the fever came for you too.
ev.c_h_plague.help.success: You carried water and bread to those everyone else had abandoned. The sickness never touched you — and the city remembered.
ev.c_h_plague.help.failure: You helped others — and fell ill yourself. Now they bring the water to you.
ev.c_h_lingering.title: A Lingering Illness
ev.c_h_lingering.text: The illness has dragged on for months: your strength is going, the work is at a standstill, the family watches anxiously. It can't go on like this — time to decide in earnest.
ev.c_h_lingering.physician: Spend whatever it takes on the best physician
ev.c_h_lingering.physician.ok: The physician was expensive, stern and right. A month later you were on your feet.
ev.c_h_lingering.temple: Stay at the temple and wait for the gods' mercy
ev.c_h_lingering.temple.ok: Weeks of prayer, incense and temple broth. The illness retreated — slowly, almost reluctantly.
ev.c_h_lingering.endure.ok: You pulled through on your own, but the illness took its fee — in strength and in years.
ev.c_h_still_ill.title: The Illness Lingers
ev.c_h_still_ill.text.1: You're still ill: weakness, fever in the evenings, no appetite. The household tiptoes about and exchanges glances.
ev.c_h_still_ill.text.2: The sickness drags on. In the morning it seems better, by evening worse. It's time to do something.
ev.c_h_still_ill.physician: Call a physician, whatever it costs
ev.c_h_still_ill.physician.ok: The physician changed the draughts, forbade wine and ordered sleep until noon. Two weeks later you were up.
ev.c_h_still_ill.temple: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.c_h_still_ill.temple.success: The morning after the offering the fever didn't return. You decided not to ask why.
ev.c_h_still_ill.temple.failure: The offering was accepted, but the illness stayed. The healing gods must have a long queue.
ev.c_h_still_ill.rest.success: Two weeks of idleness and your body managed on its own. It just needed you to stay out of its way.
ev.c_h_still_ill.rest.failure: You lie there, and it doesn't get better. Just more boring.
ev.c_h_still_ill.work: Get up and work — maybe it'll pass
ev.c_h_still_ill.work.ok: You went back to work, swaying on your feet. Sometimes that helps. Sometimes it doesn't.
ev.c_h_recovered.text: One morning you woke up and realized: the illness was gone. Bread smells like bread again, and the sun is just the sun, not torture for the eyes.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.title: A Family Doctor
ev.c_h_family_doctor.text: A Greek physician who has treated your neighbors makes an offer: for a regular fee he'll look after the whole family — take pulses, advise on food and come at the first call.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.text.rome: A Greek physician who has treated your neighbors makes an offer: for a regular fee he'll look after the whole family — take pulses, advise on food and come at the first call. The old men grumble that their ancestors managed without Greeks — on cabbage and prayer.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.accept: Agree: let him look after us
ev.c_h_family_doctor.accept.ok: Now once a month the physician takes your pulse, looks at your tongue and eyes the wine disapprovingly. It costs money — and, it seems, buys years.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.temple: Thank you, we have our own gods
ev.c_h_family_doctor.temple.ok: You decided to stick with the temple: a modest offering every month and prayer are healing too, say the priests.
ev.c_h_family_doctor.refuse: Refuse: doctors are for the rich
ev.c_h_family_doctor.refuse.ok: The physician bowed out without offense. Said you'd meet again. Doctors always say that.
ev.c_h_doctor_saves.title: Caught in Time
ev.c_h_doctor_saves.text: Taking your pulse, the family physician suddenly frowned and ordered you to bed at once. Later he admitted that another week and it would have been too late.
ev.c_h_gym_invite.title: An Invitation to Train
ev.c_h_gym_invite.text: {g:A trainer from the palaestra|The keeper of a bathhouse with an exercise yard} looks you up and down: "Stooped shoulders, soft belly. Come to us — {g:running, wrestling, oil and strigil|ball games, light weights and oil rubs}. In a year you won't recognize yourself."
ev.c_h_gym_invite.join.ok: For the first week everything ached, even parts you never knew you had. Then you started to enjoy it.
ev.c_h_gym_invite.walks.ok: You decided to go everywhere on foot — to the river, to the market, out of town. Free, and no strigil required.
ev.c_h_gym_invite.decline: Decline — that belly was honestly earned
ev.c_h_gym_invite.decline.ok: {g:The trainer|She} shrugged. So did you, and went off to lunch.
ev.c_h_gym_later.title: In Good Shape
ev.c_h_gym_later.text: People your age groan getting up from a bench, while you still overtake the young on the way to market. The years of training have paid off.
ev.c_h_asclepius.title: A Night with Asclepius
ev.c_h_asclepius.text: The illness won't let go, and people point you to the temple of Asclepius at the foot of the Acropolis: the sick sleep there for a night, and the god appears in a dream — in person or as a snake — and shows the cure.
ev.c_h_asclepius.text.egypt: The illness won't let go, and people point you to the temple of Imhotep, whom the Greeks call Asclepius: the sick sleep there for a night, and the god shows the cure in a dream.
ev.c_h_asclepius.sleep: Spend the night in the temple
ev.c_h_asclepius.sleep.success: In your dream a bearded old man with a snake-twined staff came to you and told you to eat less and walk more. The priests interpreted the dream, you obeyed — and recovered.
ev.c_h_asclepius.sleep.failure: You slept all night without a single dream — just the snoring of the man on the next mat. The priests said the god must be busy.
ev.c_h_asclepius.doctors: See the temple's physicians — they heal without dreams too
ev.c_h_asclepius.doctors.ok: The temple physicians proved practical people: draughts, baths, a strict regimen. The god, they say, approved.
ev.c_h_asclepius.home: Spare the expense and go home
ev.c_h_asclepius.home.ok: You stood at the gate, breathed in the incense and went home. Maybe it'll pass anyway.
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.title: A Night with Aesculapius
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.text: The illness won't let go, and people point you to the temple of Aesculapius on the island in the Tiber: the sick sleep there for a night, and the god appears in a dream and shows the cure.
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.sleep: Spend the night in the temple
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.sleep.success: In your dream a bearded old man with a snake-twined staff came to you and told you to eat less and walk more. The priests interpreted the dream, you obeyed — and recovered.
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.sleep.failure: You slept all night without a single dream — just the snoring of the man on the next mat. The priests said the god must be busy.
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.doctors: See the temple's physicians — they heal without dreams too
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.doctors.ok: The temple physicians proved practical people: draughts, baths, a strict regimen. The god, they say, approved.
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.home: Spare the expense and go home
ev.c_h_asclepius_rome.home.ok: You stood at the gate, breathed in the incense and went home. Maybe it'll pass anyway.
ev.c_h_diet.title: The Doctor's Advice
ev.c_h_diet.text: A Greek physician you know watched you eat and delivered a whole lecture: less fatty meat and unmixed wine, more barley, greens and walking. "Moderation in all things," he concluded.
ev.c_h_diet.follow.ok: Porridge, greens, fish, long walks. The first month you missed the rich food; then you noticed you were sleeping better.
ev.c_h_diet.walks: Just the walks — the food stays
ev.c_h_diet.walks.ok: You walk for an hour every evening — and every evening you come back to a laden table.
ev.c_h_diet.feast.ok: The physician left, shaking his head. The wine was excellent.
ev.c_h_gout_later.title: Gout
ev.c_h_gout_later.text: Your big toe is swollen and burning so badly that even the touch of the sheet hurts. That same physician just spread his hands: "The disease of the well-fed. I did warn you."
ev.c_h_gout_later.diet: Go on plain food and water
ev.c_h_gout_later.diet.ok: Without wine and meat life has gone bland and the foot has gone well. You keep haggling with yourself over which matters more.
ev.c_h_gout_later.physician: Get treatment — but eat as before
ev.c_h_gout_later.physician.ok: Poultices, draughts, rest. The attack passed — until the next feast.
ev.c_h_gout_later.endure: Grit your teeth and change nothing
ev.c_h_gout_later.endure.success: Two weeks later the attack eased. You celebrated with a feast.
ev.c_h_gout_later.endure.failure: The foot hurts for months. You miss feasts now, and not by choice.
ev.c_h_aging.text.1: {g:The barber|A neighbor doing your hair} showed you your first gray hair — like evidence in court. You swore {g:him|her} to silence.
ev.c_h_aging.text.2: You have to hold the scroll farther and farther from your eyes. Soon, apparently, you'll need longer arms.
ev.c_h_aging.text.3: After a full day's work your back now aches until morning. At twenty it was never like this — or you just don't remember.
ev.c_h_back.title: A Bad Back
ev.c_h_back.text: Your back has seized up so badly you can't straighten. Friends recommend the masseur at the baths — he'll knead you, steam you, rub you with oil. The family recommends lying down and not moving.
ev.c_h_back.baths: Go to the baths every day
ev.c_h_back.baths.ok: The hot room, the cold pool, the masseur's hands — your back straightened, and you caught up on all the city gossip besides.
ev.c_h_back.walks.ok: The lame neighbor's advice turned out best: walk. You walk — and your back grows more grateful by the day.
ev.c_h_back.rest.ok: You spent a week staring at the ceiling. The back got better; the laziness, it seems, has stayed.
ev.c_h_quack.text: A trader at the market shouts that his potion cures fever, baldness, toothache and unrequited love. You didn't buy any, but you enjoyed listening — the show was better than the theater.
